title: Neural Network
subtitle: Forward pass, backpropagation, and what activations do
library: hand-written numpy (pandas for I/O, sklearn as a cross-check oracle only)

activations.name: sigmoid
activations.note: Saturates at both ends, where the derivative falls to almost zero and learning stalls. Still the natural choice for a binary output, where a probability is wanted.

activations.name: tanh
activations.note: Zero-centred, and its peak slope is 1.0 against sigmoid's 0.25, so gradients survive better through a stack of layers. Still saturates in both tails.

activations.name: relu
activations.note: No saturation on the positive side, so deep stacks train far faster. A unit pushed permanently negative has zero gradient for every input and stops learning -- a 'dead' unit.

activations.name: leaky_relu
activations.note: ReLU with a shallow slope kept on the negative side, so a unit that goes negative still receives some gradient and can recover.

activations.name: elu
activations.formula: f(z) = z if z > 0 else e^z - 1
activations.note: Smooth at the origin and saturates gently to -1, which keeps activations closer to zero-centred than ReLU does.

activations.name: gelu
activations.derivative: f'(z) — smooth, dips below 0 near the origin
activations.note: A smooth ReLU that weights the input by how likely it is to be kept. The default in most current transformer models.
